source_caption:
The iconic “kiss of death” scene in The Godfather Part II seals Fredo’s tragic fate. However, this dark narrative trajectory sparked a major creative dispute behind the scenes. Original author Mario Puzo vehemently opposed director Francis Ford Coppola’s decision to have Michael orchestrate the murder of his own brother, arguing that such a profound act of familicide was fundamentally implausible and violated the core mafia code of family loyalty. Coppola remained adamant that Michael’s complete moral descent required it, leading the two collaborators to strike a precise compromise: Puzo agreed to allow Fredo’s execution to be written into the script, but only on the strict condition that Michael would wait to issue the kill order until after their mother, Carmela, had died.

The Godfather Part II (1974), directed by Francis Ford Coppola, starring Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Robert Duvall, John Cazale. The continuing saga of the Corleone crime family tells the parallel stories of Michael Corleone’s moral descent as he expands his syndicate in 1958, and the early 20th-century rise of his father, Vito Corleone, from a Sicilian immigrant to a powerful New York mob boss.

source_details.title: The Godfather Part II
source_details.synopsis: The Godfather Part II is a 1974 American epic gangster film produced and directed by Francis Ford Coppola, loosely based on the 1969 novel The Godfather by Mario Puzo, who co-wrote the screenplay with Coppola. It is both a sequel and a prequel to the 1972 film The Godfather, presenting two parallel dramas: one picks up the 1958 story of Michael Corleone (Al Pacino), the new Don of the Corleone family, protecting the family business in the aftermath of an attempt on his life; the other covers the journey of his father, Vito Corleone (Robert De Niro), from his Sicilian childhood to the founding of his family enterprise in New York City. The ensemble cast also features Robert Duvall, Diane Keat
